title: Self-service sign-up: a stranger asks for a workspace, with no manual or infra step
description: The owner's acceptance scenario (T-2749, G10b, acceptance map item 11 'self-service demo tenant'). The runner calls the PUBLIC sign-up routes without a token (actor 'anonymous'), with a throwaway address in the mail trap (Mailpit) and a uat-tmp-* company name. Part 1 (this file, runs on today's build): S1 the sign-up is switched on and its config is public; S2 a request without accepted terms is refused 422 invalid_request naming terms_accepted; S3 a request with a malformed address is refused 422; S4 a good request is answered 202 check_your_mail; S5 the verification mail reaches the trap (wait_mail: the body and the token never reach the log). Part 2 (see later_steps) needs the sign-up fields slug, user name and password of T-2748 and the one-time provisioner wiring on QA: until they exist the whole file is blocked_by them and the runner reports it as NOT RUN, never as a pass and never as a failure. D-195: the scenario goes from the sign-up to a signed-in tenant admin with no step that waits for a human; a step that does is a defect and a red scenario, named in the verdict line. No qoimeks-qa or qoimeks-client1-qa tenant is touched. The verification link is opened by the SPA page, so the runner does not read the body of the mail. Part 2 is executable: S6 posts the full sign-up (company name, user name, password from the input signup_password, slug uat-tmp-<run_id>) and expects 202 with the tenant URL; a closed refusal such as demo_cap_reached (409 limit, the cap reached) fails S6 and the verdict line names it (the cap is never filled on purpose; the regression test drives S6 with that answer). S7 the platform administrator reads the registry entry and expects status active with no human step (D-195). S8 slug taken and S9 reserved slug are refused. S10 signs in as the NEW tenant admin (password grant in the new realm uat-tmp-<run_id>; the token is a secret, never logged) and S11 reads GET /api/v1/me/access with that token and expects the role TENANT_ADMIN. The cleanup deactivates ONLY the tenant uat-tmp-<run_id> and always runs (200 or 404 when the sign-up made nothing), so a sign-up that created the tenant but failed an assertion is still reconciled; the platform residue check (actor admin on the platform tenant) fails the run on a leftover active uat-tmp-* tenant. Removing blocked_by is an acceptance line of T-2748 / T-2728 and the provisioner wiring: the task that builds the last piece removes it. The realm is read from the registry entry (idp_realm_id), never derived from the slug.
later_steps: L5b: purge of the tenant after the deactivation, only when T-2747 exists

inputs.signup_password: <set by the starter at run time>

dry_run.blocked_by: T-2748 (sign-up screens and fields), T-2728 (platform routes 3/4) and the QA provisioner wiring (infra draft, owner's go): the task that builds the last piece removes this marker and the scenario goes green in the same PR

steps.says: Anyone may read the public sign-up config: it is switched on and offers the three languages. If it answers 404 the sign-up is not enabled on this build: RED, reason 'sign-up not enabled'.
A request that does not accept the terms is refused 422 and names the field.
A good request is answered 202 check_your_mail, whether or not the address is known.
The verification mail reaches the throwaway address in the mail trap, with no human step. Only recipient, subject and message id are read.

The full sign-up: company name, user name, password, desired slug. Answered 202 with the tenant URL of the new workspace. A red here, once unblocked, means the build lacks the sign-up fields (T-2748) or the provisioner is not configured.
With no human step the new tenant exists and is active (the platform administrator reads the registry entry). D-195: if it waits for a person it is RED.
The slug is taken: a second sign-up for the same slug is refused with the code slug_taken.
A reserved word as the slug is refused 422.

Sign in as the NEW tenant admin in the realm the registry names (the provisioner issues it, it is not the slug), with the password given at sign-up and no step by a person (D-195). No token in the log.
The tenant opens for its new administrator: the access list answers 200 with the role TENANT_ADMIN.

cleanup.says: Deactivate only the throwaway tenant this run may have made (slug uat-tmp-<run_id>, never a permanent one). Runs after a failed sign-up too: 404 means nothing was made.
